description.narrative: The Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (TRA) of Lebanon has requested World Bank support to build its capacity to become an efficient 21st-century regulatory authority that is transparent, responsive, and technically competent. Proposed activities are proposed to be funded by an IDF grant, and will include developing and integrating various processes and procedures, both internal, vis-à-vis third parties, and vertically and horizontally across the organization, including utilizing electronic means. Many of these processes and procedures are related to TRA#s functions as described in the law. Some of the processes and procedures will include TRA#s docketing procedures for its various activities. The capacity-building project will also need to take account of certain underlying legal and regulatory issues regarding the establishment of the legal equivalence of on-line transactions (legal recognition of electronic contracting, electronic documents and issues dealing with on-line authentication (e-signatures), rules regarding dispatch and receipt of electronic messages, data base management and security (and privacy) of electronic transactions among others). Other activities to be included are: Defining roles and responsibilities within TRA and among Board Members; Conversion of analogue, paper-based processes and procedures to digital/electronic means; Strengthening frequency management processes and procedures, and the equipment type approval processes and procedures; Developing budget planning, implementation and monitoring; Improving metrics and Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) of activities; Improving knowledge management within the organization. This IDF grant supports the Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (TRA) of Lebanon as it (a) streamlines its internal processes, (b) strengthens external transparency, and (c) builds technical capacity on specific regulatory and policy issues. Achieving these objectives will enable TRA to be a credible, efficient, and responsive regulator for the Lebanese telecommunications sector, supporting its position as a leading force in sector reform. Improving the regulatory environment for telecommunications in Lebanon in this manner will unlock significant growth opportunities, both for the telecommunications industry and for the broader economy. Indeed, industry surveys, regional benchmarking, and the Government's own targets suggest that further reforms can lead telephony and Internet services to reach a significantly larger population. Improved sector performance will also accelerate economic growth and create social development opportunities. Hence, the proposed IDF grant will assist TRA create a more efficient telecommunications sector that will attract investments, create jobs, and help rebuild the Lebanese economy.
